known_defects.defect: box->wlp (`backup path`) and box->bond0 (`eno1 2.5 GbE`) leave the host as two parallel horizontal runs two rows apart, so each label sits immediately above the other's route; the association relies on the renderer's label-above-route convention rather than on separation

known_defects.mitigation: each arrowhead lands on a distinct node and each label sits directly above its own run, so the reading is recoverable; both routes are audited separately

blockers.capability_missing: no edge style for a blocked or absent path
blockers.detail: `style` accepts solid or dashed only, and dashed means an unconfirmed link. The source's `no global IPv6 => v6 internet unreachable from this host` is a negative reachability claim; drawing it as a dashed edge would assert an unconfirmed link that does not exist.
blockers.workaround: carried as the host node label `v6 ULA` (abbreviated) plus this ledger entry; not faked as a link

blockers.capability_missing: no property/annotation channel for measured path attributes
blockers.detail: `bench internet` answers (NAT on egress, no committed rate, no v6) are properties of one measured path, not links between nodes; nodes and edges only carry labels, so `no committed rate` has nowhere honest to go
blockers.workaround: NAT is drawn on e11, no-v6 on the host label, no-committed-rate recorded here only

blockers.detail: `trunks` works (probe/trunk-probe-*.json: `trunks: lan from rtr to bond0, 1 branches`, extent 48x27), but a trunk draws one corridor out of `from` plus unlabelled spurs. The only genuine shared bus in this source is the home LAN, and both of its links emit from the NICs toward the router, so every trunk form reversed e9/e10 or invented a wlp<->bond0 link; spurs also have no label field, so `default 0.5 ms` and `metric 600` would be lost.
blockers.secondary_findings: a trunk also needs at least one declared edge (a trunk-only spec is rejected) and failed to route without an empty spacer layer (`no obstacle-safe route for rtr -> wlp`)
blockers.workaround: not used, documented instead of faked; the failover contrast is carried by two labelled edges in v2
